question.problem: The area of the rectangle is increasing. The base of the rectangle is $b,$ and its height is $10$ times its base. Find the rate of change of the area of a rectangle with respect to its base.
question.worked_solution:
The area of a rectangle is given by  

$$
A=bh,
$$

 where $b$ is the base and $h$ is the height of the rectangle.

We are given that $h=10b,$ so we can express the area $A$ as a function of the base $b$ by substituting $h=10b$ in the formula above. We get

$$
A=b(10b)=10{b}^{2}.
$$

Therefore, the rate of change of $A(b)$  with respect to $b$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{′}(b) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}b}(10{b}^{2}) \\  & =10\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}b}({b}^{2}) \\  & =10(2b) \\  & =20b.\end{aligned}
$$
